feed.title: Ruberto Lab @ FSU
feed.subtitle: Our team brings together expertise in cellular and molecular biology, multi-omics, high-content imaging, and drug discovery to investigate pathogen biology and treatment response. We study the development, persistence, drug resistance, and therapeutic vulnerabilities of parasites and other human pathogens. Through collaborative and interdisciplinary research, we aim to identify new biological targets and support the development of more effective treatments for infectious diseases.

entry.title: Welcome Dr. Malhotra
entry.content:
We are pleased to welcome Dr. Rashim Malhotra to the Ruberto Lab as a Postdoctoral Research Associate.

Dr. Malhotra earned her PhD in Dr. Krishanpal Karmodiya’s laboratory at the Indian Institute of Science Education and Research (IISER) Pune, India. Her doctoral research focused on RNA biology and gene regulation in Plasmodium falciparum, particularly the role of RNA-mediated mechanisms in parasite adaptation to stress.

She recently published a study titled “Sense-Antisense RNA duplexes mediate stress-responsive translational control in Plasmodium falciparum” in the journal RNA (DOI: 10.1261/rna.081149.126).

entry.title: The Ruberto Lab Officially Launches!
entry.content:
We are excited to announce the official launch of the Ruberto Laboratory on May 1, 2026, in the Department of Biomedical Sciences at Florida State University College of Medicine!

The Ruberto Lab investigates eukaryotic parasites responsible for diseases of major public health importance. By integrating parasitology, functional genomics, and drug discovery, we aim to uncover mechanisms of parasite survival and drug resistance and identify new therapeutic strategies.

We look forward to building a collaborative and interdisciplinary research environment, mentoring the next generation of scientists, and sharing our discoveries as the laboratory grows.

Stay tuned for updates on our research, publications, and laboratory activities!
